items.title: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
items.description: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at the airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes on 4 August.

items.title: US strikes Iran as state media reports four killed at wedding party
items.description: Iranian news agencies said retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US targets had begun.

items.title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
items.description: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.

items.title: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
items.description: Major efforts to rescue hydropower workers continue as Nepal's death toll exceeds 1,000.

items.title: Sexual assaults happening almost every day in Ceuta, prosecutors say
items.description: Most migrants have returned to neighbouring Morocco, but as many as 5,000 remain in the Spanish exclave.

items.title: Jurors in Lindsay Clancy trial deadlocked but judge asks them to keep trying
items.description: The Massachusetts mother is facing murder charges for killing her three children at their family home in 2023.

items.title: Ariana Grande completes tour and steps back from public life
items.description: The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".

items.title: Pistol in a lake gives hope for French cold case
items.description: Saad al-Hilli was shot dead with his wife and mother-in-law while holidaying in eastern France in September 2012.

items.title: As Michigan Senate race heats up, Vance calls El-Sayed 'evil'
items.description: El-Sayed faces Trump ally Mike Rogers in what has quickly become a senate race characterised by personal attacks and insults between the two.

items.title: France targets Shein and Temu with fast fashion fees
items.description: The levy on "ultra-fast fashion" items could reach almost €20 per garment by 2030.

items.title: 'I have fired 40 of my agents for being corrupt', says Nigeria's anti-corruption chief
items.description: The EFCC boss says more than five of the dismissed officials are already facing prosecution.

items.title: Israel says Hamas security chief captured as strikes kill four during Gaza raid
items.description: The Israeli military says it carried out strikes in Gaza City during a raid by special forces to capture the head of Hamas's internal security service.

items.title: Trump says US position on Falklands 'one of many' under review
items.description: The UK says Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future".

items.title: Ex-gang boss guilty of orchestrating 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur
items.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis was convicted over the drive-by shooting of the rap superstar 30 years ago.

items.title: Russian attack hits rail workers in new deadly strikes on Kyiv
items.description: Ukrainian officials say 20 people, including two children, were injured in the capital and the wider region.

items.title: Shein valued at $26bn after long-awaited stock market debut
items.description: The firm's Hong Kong listing on Tuesday comes after a years-long quest to sell shares in New York and London.

items.title: Woman killed in Times Square stabbing, suspect shot dead by police
items.description: Police say the double stabbing, which injured another person, was random and the suspect had a mental health history.

items.title: Amazon rigged $20bn worth of ad prices, US lawsuit alleges
items.description: Amazon responded to the lawsuit, arguing the US Federal Trade Commission "misunderstands" their ad market.

items.title: Teen girl charged with murder over recording of San Diego mosque attack
items.description: Prosecutors say the 17-year-old from North Carolina also published a manifesto from the two teenage shooters in the 18 May attack.

items.title: South Korean police officer admits to closing missing person cases to avoid work
items.description: The officer falsely claimed he contacted missing persons and prematurely closed their cases on the South Korean holiday island of Jeju.
